description_full: A10 Networks, Inc. provides secure application and network infrastructure solutions in the United States, the rest of Americas, Japan, rest of the Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The company offers security products, such as ThreatX, a web application protection platform; A10 Defend DDoS Detector, a network-wide anomaly detection product; A10 Defend DDoS Orchestrator, a defense, orchestration, and management product; A10 Defend DDoS Mitigator, a mitigation product with automation; A10 Defend Threat Control, an attack SaaS platform; and Defend Next-Gen WAF, an integrated application delivery and web application firewall. It also provides infrastructure products, including A10 Thunder ADC, an application delivery controller and load balancer; A10 Thunder CFW, a consolidated network security platform with stateful firewall, IPsec VPN, CGN, ADC, SSLi, and secure web gateway; A10 Thunder CGN, a NAT, IPv4 preservation and IPv6 migration product; and SSL insight in Thunder CFW, a TLS and SSL decryption for real-time visibility into encryption traffic under the SSLi brand. In addition, the company provides centralized management and analytics comprising A10 Control, a centralized, management, control, and analytics platform for agile operations and automation. It serves telecommunications, technology, financial services, public sector, industrial, retail, gaming, and education industries through distribution channels, distributors, value added resellers, and system integrators. The company was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: A10 Networks, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $2.1B market cap on $291M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +3.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 85% against a 9% cost of capital — a 76-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 78% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $65M in free cash flow — roughly 22 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.01× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 8.0×.

Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 16% operating margin runs 9pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 68% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 26% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 42% and a beta of 1.00, it moves roughly with the market.
About $28.0M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 52% in the 2020 crash and 23% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $27.58 (margin of safety -4%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 12%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $19.84 to $38.88 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 44.8 vs 27.4 and EV/EBITDA 26.9 vs 17.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 52% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 6 covering analysts target $34.17 on average, 19% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 85% clears the cost of capital of 9.1% by 76pp, the mark of a value creator.
It runs a 78% gross margin and converts 22% of revenue into free cash flow, or 15% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.01x.
ROE of 20% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (3.0x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 14pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 23.8% of revenue on R&D and 6.9% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $159.1M (8% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.1% over 3 years, 5.2% over 5 years and 3.9% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 4.6% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.98, a backlog worth 49% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 4%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.4x, 6.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.6%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 4.2% a year to shareholders (3.3% in buybacks and 0.8% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 1.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 18.8% of the float, 9.7 days to cover.
people: With about 494 employees, each generates about $588K of revenue, 1.6x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 4.5% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $131K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.8M (3x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (9/10, lower is better).
